why: A vehicle cutting into the ego lane then braking is my new hazard. NHTSA 100-Car Phase II reports 64 near-crashes and 324 incidents with a cut-in ahead among about 2,025,000 miles (DOT HS 810 593, Goal 6, https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/100carmain.pdf; top-level mileage also reported in Table 2.7). I use (64+324)/2,025,000 × 12 miles/trip = 0.00230 per trip as a deliberately generous proxy for cut-ins that also brake; this is not a direct estimate of the narrower combined event. The sampled brake range 0.8–1.5 m/s² is about 0.08–0.15 g and matches the NHTSA naturalistic lead-deceleration range of 0.05–0.15 g (https://www.nhtsa.gov/document/modeling-driver-response-lead-vehicle-decelerating); the duration and trigger ranges are scenario design ranges inside avsim/studio.py LIMITS, not measured population distributions. The conservative exposure likely overstates frequency of the combined event; a local naturalistic fleet dataset with event labels and odometer distance is needed to estimate it directly.
